pr_comment: Hi @piergm, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
I'm really excited that this is happening. Thanks for working on it ❤️

I wonder if it's possible to make these changes without touching ContentPath, which is getting considerably more complicated here.  I think we can keep all our changes within `DocumentParser#parseObjectDynamic`, and do something like: if we have a dynamically created object mapper here but subobjects are disallowed, then throw said object mapper away and instead create a new DocumentParserContext with a wrapped XContentParser that prepends the current field name to any of its immediate children, and pass this to `parseObjectOrField`.  I think this would also simplify the handling of the dynamic runtime case: where we currently create a fake object mapper for the context to use, we instead modify the xcontentparser to include the extra field level when it reports field names but stick with the same ObjectMapper parent.

Have a look at XContentSubParser to get an idea of how this might be implemented - keep track of the nesting level, and if we're at level 1 when `currentName()` is called, return the delegate name with the extra field name prepended, otherwise just delegate.

That is because service.time is mapped, but not as an object. It did run because of a bug discovered thanks to your comment above. 
Ref:
> I would expect this to break things, as it effectively ignores the subobjects setting at each object level (it can be set within any object)

Got it. This is the third problem we discussed. When you do have an object in the document, and the field is mapped but not as an object, there are cases in which you do need to provide the object as-is to the mapper for parsing (e.g. geo_point) and the majority of the cases in which you can just throw an error (e.g. because long does not support parsing objects). We are covered for the error situation, that happens already, but we need to cover the geo_point scenario, and we don't have a systematic way to say: "does the mapper support parsing objects?". We should avoid instanceof checks and rather introduce a way to discriminate between mappers that can and cannot parse objects natively.

So, if I understood correctly, when `subobject: false` we want to be able to provide the entire object as-is to the mapper for parsing if either:

1. There is a dynamic template for such field or 
2. There is a mapped field of any type that can natively parse objects.

While in the case of this particular test, where there is a mapped field but the type cannot parse objects, we just want an exception.

Did I understood correctly or am I missing something?

I tripped on the following sentence:

> While in the case of this particular test, where there is a mapped field but the type cannot parse objects, we just want an exception.

Not, we want to parse its sub-fields and ignore their object container. That is one of the challenges of this change. Sorry about the confusion.
